ledger.note: 989: Landry of Monceaux becomes the first hereditary Count of Nevers. The page says he was the first hereditary count, serving 'from 989 to 1028', and that around 990 his father-in-law Otto-William, who had administered the Nivernais, granted him Nevers with the consent of Duke Henry I and King Hugh Capet. The List page gives Landry 992-1028 and puts Otto-Henry (c. 973-987) and Otto-William (987-992) before him; the County page says only that 'The county itself dates from approximately the beginning of the 10th century'. The Nivernais page: the province roughly coincides with the later Duchy of Nevers and forms the modern department of Nièvre, which is the region used.

1002: Landry takes Auxerre in the succession war over the duchy. The Auxerre page lists 'Landerich of Monceau, 1002-1028' as count; the Landry page says he supported Otto-William and occupied Auxerre during the 1002-1005 conflict. Cliopatria keeps Auxerre in Nevers from 1010.

1003: King Robert II's army fails before Auxerre. The page says that in 1003 Robert's armed intervention, with Norman troops, failed in front of Auxerre and Saint-Germain d'Auxerre, in a rivalry over Auxerre between Bishop Hugh of Chalon and Count Landry of Nevers, Otto-William's son-in-law (paraphrase).

1005: Robert II makes peace with Landry after two unsuccessful sieges of Auxerre and the surrounding area (the page's account, paraphrased; Robert had called on Duke Richard II of Normandy for troops). The Robert II page adds that Landry was reconciled by giving up the counties of Avallon and Auxerre; the Auxerre page lists him as count of Auxerre to 1028 and Cliopatria keeps Auxerre in the Nevers shape: the pages disagree, so no loss of Auxerre is recorded.

1031: Renaud I succeeds Landry (the Auxerre page has Renauld from 1028). The County page: 'Beginning with Renauld I, the county was held jointly with that of the County of Auxerre'; the List page marks Renaud I and the counts after him 'also Count of Auxerre' to 1262. Renaud I married Adwisa, daughter of King Robert II (Landry page).

1184: Peter II of Courtenay, husband of Countess Agnes I (1181-1192), shares the county; the Courtenay house enters the line (List page: Peter II 1184-1192; the Auxerre page has him as count of Auxerre 1184-1218).
1199: Hervé IV of Donzy enters the line beside Matilda I (countess 1192-1257); the List page gives Hervé 1199-1223 and Guigues IV of Forez 1226-1241 without stating their relation to her.
1257: Matilda II and her husband Odo of Burgundy hold the county (List page: both 1257-1262, also counts of Auxerre); Yolande II follows in 1262-1280.

region.text: the County of Auxerre (Auxerre and its surroundings)

ledger.note: 1262: the Auxerre line separates from Nevers. County of Auxerre page (opened 2026-11-01): Mahaut of Dampierre and Odo of Burgundy are counts of Auxerre '1257-1262' (the same couple hold Nevers 1257-1262, ledger/7); the page's later counts of Auxerre are Alix of Burgundy and John I ('1273-1290, joint rulers'), William VI (1290-1304), John II (1304-1361) and John III (1361-1370), none of them in the Nevers list (Yolande II 1262-1280, Robert III of Flanders 1272-1280, Louis I of Flanders 1280-1322), and 'Count John IV sold it to the King of France in 1370' (the Crown lands page used by royal-domain-of-france ledger/34 has 1371). The year is the end of Odo and Mahaut's joint rule; the page does not say who held Auxerre in 1262-1273. The 30 km disc is the one royal-domain-of-france and burgundian-state use. [fx-30 2026-11-01, finding F252: added; the dossier drew Auxerre as Nevers land to 1539.]

1272: Robert III of Flanders holds the county (List page: Robert III 1272-1280, count of Flanders 1305-1322; father of Louis I, who follows in 1280-1322). Cliopatria draws the Nièvre inside the Flanders shape 1272-1284.

region.text: the County of Nevers with Rethel

ledger.note: 1322: Louis I of Flanders becomes Count of Nevers and Flanders; the county is ruled with Flanders until 1384. The Louis I of Flanders page says 'He succeeded his father as count of Nevers and his grandfather as count of Flanders in 1322' and that he was killed at Crécy in 1346. Cliopatria's Nevers row ends in 1325 and the Flanders shape covers the Nièvre from 1326. The List page lists Louis II of Flanders as Count of Nevers 1346-1384.

region.text: the counties of Nevers and Rethel

ledger.note: 1384: Nevers and Rethel pass to Philip the Bold with the Flanders inheritance: 'Cet héritage est réalisé en 1384', covering Flanders, the County of Burgundy and 'des comtés de Nevers et de Rethel (fiefs français)'. The List page has John the Fearless count of Nevers 1384-1404. Cliopatria draws the Nièvre inside the Duchy of Burgundy shape 1385-1406.

1407: Philip II takes Nevers and Rethel as his own. 'both held by Philip's younger son Philip II from 1407'. The Philip II page's infobox gives Nevers from 1404 and Rethel from 1406; Cliopatria draws the split in 1407 and the ledger follows it.

1491: the Cleves line takes the county. Engelbert 'became Count of Nevers and Eu in 1491 upon the death of his maternal grandfather John II, Count of Nevers' (his mother was Elizabeth of Nevers). Eu lies outside the Nevers shape; the page does not say whether Rethel stayed with the county.

1539: the county of Nevers is raised to a duchy in the peerage of France. 'The count was raised to duke in 1539' (County page); the List page: 'In 1539, it became a duchy in the peerage of France', François I the first duke (1539-1561). The duchy survived 'until the French Revolution' but is not drawn as a separate state; Cliopatria has the Nièvre inside the Kingdom of France from 1521.

wars.name: Succession war for the Duchy of Burgundy
wars.outcome: Two unsuccessful royal sieges of Auxerre and its area; Robert II made peace with Landry in 1005.
wars.note: Landry backed Otto-William; Robert II called on Duke Richard II of Normandy, who sent 30,000 soldiers (page). The Robert II page says Landry gave up Auxerre and Avallon.

wars.name: Battle of Agincourt
wars.outcome: Count Philip II of Nevers and Rethel was killed on 25 October 1415; his son Charles I, born 1414, succeeded. No land changed hands.

certainty.note: A feudal county with no treaty or survey line on any page; the outline is the Nivernais with the Auxerre area, as Cliopatria draws it.

notes:
Written for eu-10-e from the nine pages of the budget (County of Nevers, List of counts and dukes of Nevers, Nivernais, Louis I of Flanders, Philip II, Charles I, County of Auxerre, Landry, Engelbert) and, for the Burgundian events, the Burgundian Netherlands, French Duchy and Robert II pages already opened for the Duchy of Burgundy dossier. Three of the nine are thin (County of Nevers and Nivernais are stubs, Charles I names no territorial event), so the ledger rests on the List and on the other biographies. No page gives an area; no infobox comparison was possible.
START AND END: Cliopatria's row is 1010-1520. The Landry page puts the first hereditary count at 989, so the dossier starts there with a new keyframe 989-1009 (overlapping the Duchy of Burgundy shape, which draws the Nièvre in 1003-1009). The row ends in 1520 because the Kingdom of France shape covers the Nièvre from 1521; the pages have Charles II to 1521, François I 1521-1539 and the county raised to a duchy in 1539, so the dossier ends in 1539 with the Cliopatria shape carried forward 1521-1539 (new keyframe). The Duchy of Nevers 1539-1790 is not given a dossier; if the orchestrator wants it, it is a rename of this state, not a new one.
DORMANT SPANS (personal union): 1322-1406 the county is ruled with Flanders (1322-1384, Louis I and Louis II of Flanders) and then by the dukes of Burgundy (1384-1407). Cliopatria has no Nevers row 1326-1406 and draws the Nièvre in the Flanders shape and then in the Duchy of Burgundy shape (25 of 28 cells, then 28 of 28). The ledger records merge 1322 and merge 1384, then gain 1407; there are no keyframes in between. Likewise 1272-1284 (Cliopatria: inside Flanders) gets a carried keyframe because the List page has Robert III and Louis I as counts.
